D-283 and D-284 are dispositive on the obvious rebuttal. Both faced exactly this situation — a turn-1 finding that landed at turn 2, reaching turn 3 — and the corpus did not leave it to inference: it wrote a clause for it. The 'carried, not re-landed' sentence exists in those two entries for no other purpose.

Internal asymmetry within this entry. Every other named identifier carries a disposition: Stage A v7 OB-1/OB-2/OB-3 'travel as honesty work'; Stage A v6 SF-1/SF-2 'landed at g30 leftover-join.v7'; Stage A v6 OB-1/OB-2 'travel as honesty work of the frozen predecessor'; Stage B turn-1 CLAUDE-D319-O1/O2/O3 'they travel as honesty work'; Stage B turn-2 CLAUDE-D319-T2-O-1..O-4 'they travel as honesty work'; Stage B turn-2 CLAUDE-D319-T2-SF1 'Lands'. Only CLAUDE-D319-S1 and CLAUDE-D319-S2 have none.

Aggravating context, not separately charged: the only standing clause that trails the S1/S2 mention is 'they travel as honesty work', closing the enumeration that contains 'a 2-member shouldFix list CLAUDE-D319-S1 CLAUDE-D319-S2'. Under the corpus reading (D-313, D-317, D-318) 'they' attaches to the observations, which is why I do not charge that sentence — it is the repair I prescribed at turn 2. But the effect is that the nearest disposition to S1 and S2 is one that, misread, recharacterises two landed findings as undischarged honesty work: the precise defect CLAUDE-D319-S2 was raised to cure at turn 1.

This is not a rebuttal-by-inference case either. The corpus refuses the inference 'the cycle reached dual CONSENT, so everything landed' — otherwise D-260, D-272, D-283, D-284, D-294, D-295 and D-303 would each carry a redundant sentence.
